title: Coherent modules under a closed immersion of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth], quasi-compact, and quasi-separated; the last two conditions mean that every open cover has a finite subcover and the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Modules are on the small etale ringed site, with quasi-coherence as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. On a locally Noetherian space, coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ for the locus of nonzero geometric stalks, with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A closed immersion is representable and a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]; reduced means that etale scheme charts have local rings without nonzero nilpotents, and irreducible means nonempty and not the union of two proper closed subsets. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion and assume $X$ is Noetherian. Then $Z$ is Noetherian. The module direct image $i_*$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] takes coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-modules to coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules. For every coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $M$, one has $\operatorname{Supp}(i_*M)=|i|(\operatorname{Supp}(M))$.

proof.text: Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. The base change $V=Z\times_XU\to Z$ is surjective etale and $j:V\to U$ is a closed immersion of schemes. The scheme $U$ is locally Noetherian by the hypothesis on charts of $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft], $j$ is locally of finite type, so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $V$ locally Noetherian. For any etale scheme chart $W\to Z$, form $W'=W\times_ZV$. Its map to $W$ is a surjective etale cover, and its map to $V$ is etale. By the definitions, an etale map is locally finitely presented, hence locally of finite type: an algebra presented by finitely many generators and relations is generated by those generators. Thus [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $W'$ locally Noetherian, and [lem-trf-etale-local-noetherian-descent] makes $W$ locally Noetherian. This proves local Noetherianity of $Z$ on every chart.

The closed immersion $V\to U$ with $U$ affine identifies $V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ for $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence $V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Its atlas map $V\to Z$ is continuous and surjective on point spaces, so [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] gives quasi-compactness of $|Z|$.

By [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], $i$ is separated, so its relative diagonal $\Delta_{Z/X}$ is a closed immersion. Its base change to an affine scheme $T$ is a closed immersion into $T$, so its source is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. As in [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], regard all spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; quasi-separatedness of $X$ is quasi-compactness of its absolute diagonal on scheme tests. For a space, quasi-compactness of its point space and existence of a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme agree by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] and the last clause of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. By [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests], a morphism quasi-compact on affine scheme tests is quasi-compact on quasi-compact scheme tests and stays so after every algebraic-space base change. Hence for a quasi-compact space $C$ over its target, with atlas $C'\to C$ from a quasi-compact scheme, the pullback over $C'$ is quasi-compact; it maps surjectively etale onto the pullback over $C$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and composing with its quasi-compact scheme atlas shows that the latter is quasi-compact. So $\Delta_{Z/X}$ and the diagonal of $X$ are quasi-compact in the sense of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products]: $i$ and $X$ are quasi-separated there. Its source clause, applied to $i$, makes $Z$ quasi-separated in that sense, which includes the scheme tests of the item since quasi-compact schemes are quasi-compact spaces. Together with steps 1 and 2, $Z$ is Noetherian.

Let $M$ be coherent on $Z$. In particular it is quasi-coherent. The functor in [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules] therefore makes $i_*M$ quasi-coherent on $X$, with its scalar action through $\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$.

For any etale scheme chart $a:T\to X$, put $T_Z=Z\times_XT$ and write $j_T:T_Z\to T$. Both schemes are locally Noetherian by step 1 and the hypothesis on $X$. The restriction $M|_{T_Z}$ corresponds to a coherent Zariski module $N$ on $T_Z$, by the definition of coherence. Etale restriction of direct image [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] gives $(i_*M)|_T\simeq j_{T,*}(M|_{T_Z})$. Since a closed immersion is affine (hence quasi-compact) and separated, the direct-image clause of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies this with the etale module associated to the Zariski direct image $j_{T,*}N$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] makes $j_{T,*}N$ coherent. We have proved coherence on every chart; together with step 4, this is exactly coherence of $i_*M$.

proof.text: Use the atlas $p:U\to X$ and $q:V\to Z$ of step 1. Let $N$ be the coherent Zariski module on $V$ associated to $M|_V$. By the same direct-image comparisons as in step 5, the Zariski module of $(i_*M)|_U$ is $j_*N$. The chart support theorem and the scheme closed-support formula give $$p^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}_X(i_*M))=\operatorname{Supp}_U(j_*N)=|j|(\operatorname{Supp}_V N)=|j|(q^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}_Z M)).$$ By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], points of a fibre product map surjectively onto the fibre product of point sets. Consequently the final set equals $p^{-1}(|i|(\operatorname{Supp}_Z M))$: for $u$ with $p(u)=i(z)$ and $z$ in the support, choose a point $v$ over $(u,z)$; conversely map any such $v$ to $(u,q(v))$. Since $p$ is surjective, equality of these inverse images proves the required support formula.
